title: Developer Experience Documentation Playbook: SDKs, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Operations, and Top Support Fixes
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook defines standards and canonical content for Redwood Inference developer experience (DevEx) documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and a canonical list of top support issues with fixes. The goal is a consistent, low-friction onboarding and troubleshooting experience for engineers and ML teams integrating Redwood inference into production systems.

Intended audience
- SDK / docs engineers
- Developer advocates and solutions engineers
- Support engineers and SREs
- Product engineers who own SDKs and quickstarts

Principles (high level)
- Be authoritative: docs should be the single source of truth for usage, configuration, and troubleshooting.
- Ship runnable examples: every code sample must be copy-paste runnable with a short auth/instrumentation snippet.
- Keep quickstarts < 10 minutes to run: minimal setup, clear outputs, and CI-friendly.
- Surface cost & performance tradeoffs up-front (batching, token pricing, quantization hints).
- Track observability hooks and recommended SDK metrics for production use.

Structure of this playbook
1. SDK Guides (structure & required content)
2. Quickstarts & templates (requirements + example checklist)
3. API examples (style + canonical snippets)
4. Docs site operations (owner, CI, release cadence, tagging)
5. Top support issues & canonical fixes (triage-to-resolution flows)

1) SDK Guides — required sections and templates
Each SDK guide page (Python, TypeScript, Go, Java, etc.) must include the following top-level sections in this order:
- Quick summary (1–2 sentences)
- Installation (pip/npm/go install) with supported version matrix (table)
- Authentication (examples for API key + environment variables + recommended secrets managers)
- Minimal example (3–8 lines that returns a small response)
- Common patterns (streaming, function/tool calling, structured output parsing, embeddings)
- Configuration & performance knobs (timeouts, batching, retry policies)
- Observability & metrics (instrumentation snippet: request id propagation, latency histogram names)
- Error handling (canonical error responses and retry/backoff guidance)
- Migration notes (breaking changes between SDK versions)
- API reference link + code samples gallery
- FAQ and troubleshooting appendix

Required metadata fields for each SDK page: supported_platforms (list), sdk_version (string), last_tested_against_runtime (string, e.g., "redwood-runtime v2025.12"), maintainer (name), ci_job (path to repo job). Put these in the page header and update on releases.

Example minimal Python section (must be runnable):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate("Write a two-line haiku about latency")
print(resp.text)
```
Notes: ensure example uses environment var placeholder and prints structured response.

2) Quickstarts and templates — checklist and canonical templates
Every quickstart should hit the following acceptance criteria: 
- Time to first result: <= 10 minutes on a dev machine with free tier credentials
- Minimal friction: only one external dependency install step preferred
- CI runnable: maintained runnable test that executes a smoke test in < 90s
- Clear expected output: include sample output or hashes to validate success
- Cost & perf callouts: short paragraph about latency, token costs, and suggested model variants

Canonical quickstart templates (required):
- Text generation (Python + JS)
- Chat / system + user messages (Python + JS)
- Embeddings: indexing toy dataset + nearest-neighbor search (Python)
- Reranking example (Node)
- Function / tool calling example (Python)
- On-prem deployment smoke test (curl + small Docker Compose)

Quickstart CI pattern
1. smoke-test.yml (GitHub Actions) — checks out, installs, runs smoke.py, compares output to expected.json
2. security-scan.yml — runs tfsec / trivy for templates that include infra
3. nightly-integration.yml — optional, runs longer tests against staging runtime

3) API examples — style guide and canonical snippets
Style guide
- Keep examples focused (single feature per snippet).
- Avoid long prose; show request, response, and short notes on fields.
- Provide both REST + SDK examples for common flows.
- Mark streaming examples and include a terminal-based consumer sample.

Canonical snippets to include across repo:
- REST: token-based call for /v1/generate with streaming chunk handling (curl + Node fetch)
- SDK: minimal generate, streaming, embeddings, and batch/embed patterns
- Error handling: showing 429 (rate limit), 5xx fallback to cheaper model, and idempotency token usage
- Observability: injecting X-Request-ID, collecting upstream_latency_ms, model_variant, and token_count metrics

REST example (curl + simple JSON response expectation):
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-v1-small","prompt":"Summarize the following: ...","max_tokens":64}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate | jq .
```

4) Docs site operating procedures (owners, CI, release cadence, SLOs)
Owners and rotation
- Primary owner: devex-docs-team@redwood (team rotation)
- On-call docs engineer: weekly rota (person listed in page header)
- Escalation: contact SDK maintainer -> doc owner -> product manager if content impacts SLAs

Content lifecycle and CI
- All docs in git are the source of truth. Pull requests must include a smoke test (markdown link checks + runnable code validation).
- CI checks: link-check, code-snippets-runner (executes sandboxed examples), spell-check, linter (prettier / markdownlint). CI job names must be standardized: docs/smoke, docs/link-check, docs/snippets.
- Release cadence: publish updates to staging docs on merge; weekly public deploys on Fridays 15:00 UTC. Emergency fixes can be hotfixed with approval from the docs owner.

Versioning and deprecations
- Pages that reference specific runtime versions must include a compatibility header: (tested against redwood-runtime vYYYY.MM).
- Deprecation policy: mark deprecated features with a banner and provide migration notes; set a 90-day minimum deprecation window for breaking changes.

SLOs for docs site availability and content freshness
- Docs site uptime: 99.95% monthly (monitored by plumbing page response + health endpoint)
- Stale pages: pages with SDK metadata older than 180 days are flagged and assigned to the SDK maintainer.
- PR review SLA: minor doc PRs must be reviewed within 72 hours; security-sensitive patches must be reviewed within 24 hours.

5) Top support issues & canonical fixes (triage-first guide)
This section contains the top recurrent developer support issues reported in support tickets with canonical triage steps and fixes. Each entry includes: summary, triage steps, probable root causes, canonical fix (copy-paste), and observability checks.

Issue A: Auth failures (401 / invalid API key)
- Symptoms: immediate 401 on every request, "invalid_api_key" message
- Triage steps:
  1. Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY env var is set in process and not a placeholder.
  2. Check for accidental whitespace or newline in stored secret (e.g., from copy-paste).
  3. Verify key scopes and expiry in console (support tools link).
- Canonical fix:
  - For Linux/macOS: export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<your-key>"
  - For Docker: set env in docker-compose or pass --env REDWOOD_API_KEY accordingly
- Observability checks: request logs should show X-Auth-Status=failed with masked key_id.

Issue B: High latency on small requests (p50 > 500ms for small prompts)
- Symptoms: generation takes 500–1500ms for simple prompts; user sees UI jank
- Triage steps:
  1. Check model selection: lightweight variants (rw-v1-small) or faster endpoints recommended.
  2. Inspect batching config and client-side timeouts.
  3. Verify whether streaming vs non-streaming is used (streaming often improves perceived latency).
- Canonical fixes:
  - Use smaller model variant or enable streaming in SDK: client.stream_generate(...).
  - Configure client-side timeout and reduce top_p/temperature if sampling overhead is high.
- Observability checks: token_latency_ms and queue_wait_ms metrics on the request path.

Issue C: 429s (rate limit) during burst traffic
- Symptoms: clients receive 429 with retry-after header
- Triage steps:
  1. Confirm client is retrying with exponential backoff and jitter.
  2. Check account quota & burst limits in console.
  3. Inspect per-route rate limiting rules in gateway logs.
- Canonical fix:
  - Implement client-side retry with capped exponential backoff. Example (pseudo):
    sleep = min(base * 2**attempt + jitter(), max_backoff)
  - For predictable throughput, recommend Dedicated capacity or request quota increase.
- Observability checks: rate_limit_exceeded counter and per-user bucket metrics.

Issue D: Incorrect structured output parsing (JSON / function call mismatch)
- Symptoms: SDK returns text that is not valid JSON or function args mismatch
- Triage steps:
  1. Check prompt templates for clear "You must return JSON only" instructions.
  2. Use schema enforcement via function/tool calling APIs or parser validations.
  3. Verify model variant and temperature; higher temperature increases hallucination risk.
- Canonical fix:
  - Add validation step in the client that runs JSON.parse and on failure falls back to a deterministic parser or retries generation with lower temperature.
  - Example fallback flow: if parse fails, re-generate with system instruction: "Return ONLY valid JSON matching schema X."
- Observability checks: structured_output_failure counter, last_generation_temperature, and retry_count.

Issue E: Embedding mismatch / similarity drift after model upgrade
- Symptoms: nearest-neighbor quality drops after embeddings model was upgraded
- Triage steps:
  1. Check embedding model version and whether index was re-generated.
  2. Verify normalization and vector dimensionality.
- Canonical fix:
  - Re-index corpus with the new embeddings model and enable per-doc vector metadata for backward traceability.
  - If immediate downtime unacceptable, pin requests to the previous embedding model until a reindex job completes.
- Observability checks: embedding_model_mismatch_count, index_rebuild_status.

Documentation maintenance checklist (for support-derived updates)
- When a support issue reaches "escalated" or "bug", update the corresponding doc within 48 hours with: reproduction steps, root cause, and remediation steps.
- Link the support ticket ID in the doc (related_pages).
- Add a short note in release notes if the fix requires users to change SDK behavior or configuration.
